title: SuffixArray::construct runs the build pipeline and the builder only configures
body:
`SuffixArrayBuilder::build_to_file` (`libsufr/src/build.rs`) normalizes the text, builds the keep table, the N runs and the `PrefixEncoder`, then matches on `(fits_u32, memory_scratch)` and calls `sort_and_write::<T, B>(&self, ..)` in one of four arms. `sort_and_write` reads five fields off the builder, runs partition, sort, header and write, and returns nothing; `build_to_file` then calls `SuffixArray::open_with` on the file it wrote, which parses the header back and reads the text into a second `Vec`.

`B: ScratchBuffer` is a trait with two impls, disk and memory, threaded through eighteen signatures and `Partition<B>`. Its methods are called once per chunk and bucket in `partition`, once per partition in `sort` and `write`, never per element.

## Proposal

- The builder holds configuration only. `build_to_file` is one call: `SuffixArray::construct(path, text, sequences, alphabet, mask, max_query_len, num_partitions, write_lcp, memory_scratch, force_64bit, low_memory)`.
- `SuffixArray::construct` in `lib.rs` is the only place width is decided for a build, beside `open`, which decides it from the header. It matches `fits_u32` and calls `build::construct::<u32>` or `::<u64>`.
- `build::construct<T>(..) -> Result<Index<T>>` in `build.rs` is the pipeline top to bottom: normalize, keep table, N runs, encoder, partition, header, group, sort, first LCPs, write, then `Index::new`.
- `Index::new(path, header, text: Text, suffixes: Storage, max_query_len)` in `index.rs` opens the handles and picks the modes. `Index::open` reads the header and the text and calls it; `construct` passes the text it already holds.
- `ScratchBuffer` becomes `enum Scratch<T> { Disk(..), Memory(Vec<T>) }` with the same five methods matching inside. The `B` parameter and the four-arm match go.

The `.sufr` bytes do not change. The create benchmark runs before and after; the `Scratch` match sits at the per-chunk and per-partition call sites, not per element.

## Rejected

- The pipeline as `Index::construct` in `index.rs`: the algorithm's orchestration would sit in the file that owns opening, caching and subsampling, apart from its stages.
- The width match staying in the builder: the builder would still be the thing that builds.
